newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz German non-life unit braces to compete.
newsitem.headline: Allianz German non-life unit braces to compete.

text.p: The non-life German unit of insurance group Allianz AG said on Friday that it was expecting competition in the sector to intensify, but believed it had taken measures to equip itself for the fight.
"Even better customer service and new sales strategies are among the measures with which we intend to strengthen our market position," the unit said in a statement.

But the insurer warned that preparing for its future had dented its results in the first six months of the year, when pretax profit fell to 885 million marks from 1.002 billion a year earlier and premium income dropped by 1.9 percent.
"This is partly due to the tense economic situation in Germany, which has had a negative impact on the whole of the insurance business," the unit said.

"A further reason for this development lies in the different measures Allianz has taken to secure its market position," it added. It gave as one example a new car insurance system which allows individual discounting.

Sales to private customers developed well in the first six months, with premium income on iunsurance for legal protection, accident, third party liability and residential property growing by 6.1 percent.
But income from industrial policies fell amid intense competition and due to the implementation of risk selection systems.
The favourable claims trend seen in 1996 had deteriorated in the first half of 1997, boosted by frost and storm damage in the spring. Claims met on property insurance totalled 220 million marks.
But car insurance claims continued to fall, so that overall claims rose just 0.6 percent to 5.7 billion marks.
Capital investment rose by 2.1 billion marks to 30 billion, with earnings from this remaining at year-ago levels -- it gave no figure for the income. The workforce remained steady at 24,800.
